spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m8p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Motors, MaxRound, Nobody, InService

Isolation == [by : Banks, round : 0..MaxRound]

VARIABLES roomClaim, motorClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing

vars == <<roomClaim, motorClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ roomClaim \in Banks \cup {Nobody}
    /\ motorClaim \in [Motors -> Banks \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ isolation \in [Motors -> Isolation \cup {InService}]
    /\ permitRound \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ standing \subseteq Banks

Init ==
    /\ roomClaim = Nobody
    /\ motorClaim = [m \in Motors |-> Nobody]
    /\ isolation = [m \in Motors |-> InService]
    /\ permitRound = 0
    /\ standing = Banks

TakeRoom(b) ==
    /\ b \in standing
    /\ roomClaim = Nobody
    /\ roomClaim' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<motorClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

\* Coarse before fine: no motor claim without the machine-room claim.
TakeMotor(b, m) ==
    /\ roomClaim = b
    /\ motorClaim[m] = Nobody
    /\ motorClaim' = [motorClaim EXCEPT ![m] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

Isolate(b, m) ==
    /\ b \in standing
    /\ motorClaim[m] = b
    /\ isolation[m] = InService
    /\ isolation' = [isolation EXCEPT ![m] = [by |-> b, round |-> permitRound]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, motorClaim, permitRound, standing>>

Restore(b, m) ==
    /\ isolation[m] # InService
    /\ isolation[m].by = b
    /\ isolation' = [isolation EXCEPT ![m] = InService]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, motorClaim, permitRound, standing>>

\* Dropping the coarse claim leaves the fine ones standing behind it.
DropRoom(b) ==
    /\ roomClaim = b
    /\ roomClaim' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<motorClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

Orphaned == roomClaim = Nobody /\ \E m \in Motors : motorClaim[m] # Nobody

ClearOrphans ==
    /\ Orphaned
    /\ motorClaim' = [m \in Motors |-> Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

\* Nothing isolated under the old round survives a reissue.
Reissue ==
    /\ permitRound < MaxRound
    /\ permitRound' = permitRound + 1
    /\ isolation' = [m \in Motors |-> InService]
    /\ standing' = Banks
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, motorClaim>>

Suspend(b) ==
    /\ b \in standing
    /\ Cardinality(standing) > 1
    /\ standing' = standing \ {b}
    /\ isolation' = [m \in Motors |->
                       IF isolation[m] # InService /\ isolation[m].by = b
                         THEN InService ELSE isolation[m]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, motorClaim, permitRound>>

Next ==
    \/ ClearOrphans \/ Reissue
    \/ \E b \in Banks :
         \/ TakeRoom(b) \/ DropRoom(b) \/ Suspend(b)
         \/ \E m \in Motors : TakeMotor(b, m) \/ Isolate(b, m) \/ Restore(b, m)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(ClearOrphans)

\* Nothing is held out of service by a suspended bank or an old permit.
IsolationsAreCurrent ==
    \A m \in Motors :
        isolation[m] # InService =>
            (isolation[m].by \in standing /\ isolation[m].round = permitRound)

\* Fine claims are never left orphaned for ever.
OrphansSweptUp == Orphaned ~> ~Orphaned

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {bknorth, bksouth}
    Motors = {hm1, hm2}
    MaxRound = 1
    Nobody = nobody
    InService = inservice

INVARIANT IsolationsAreCurrent

PROPERTY OrphansSweptUp
nl:
A skyscraper has two elevator banks that run independently of one another but draw their hoist
motors from one shared machine room. Taking a motor out of service for work is done under a permit
system, and getting at a motor takes two claims, the coarse one before the fine one.

A bank's engineering desk first takes the machine-room claim, which only one of the two banks holds
at a time. Holding it, the desk may take a claim on individual motors. Only a desk holding a
motor's claim, and holding a permit, may isolate that motor; isolating records which bank did it
and which permit round was in force at the time. An isolated motor is put back into service by the
bank that isolated it.

Permits are reissued from time to time. Reissuing advances the permit round, restores every
isolated motor to service, and puts both banks back in good standing, because nothing isolated
under the old round may be left standing under the new one. A bank's permit can also be suspended
on its own, which puts back into service everything that bank had isolated; at least one bank is
always left in good standing.

Giving up the machine-room claim does not give up the motor claims taken under it, so motor claims
can be left standing with nobody holding the machine room. The building engineer sweeps up: when
the machine room is unclaimed but motor claims are still standing, they are all cleared away.

The full set of actions is: a bank in good standing takes the machine-room claim when it is free;
the bank holding the machine room takes a claim on a free motor; a bank in good standing isolates a
motor it has claimed, recording itself and the current permit round; a bank puts back into service
a motor it isolated; a bank gives up the machine-room claim, leaving its motor claims standing;
the building engineer clears away all standing motor claims while the machine room is unclaimed;
permits are reissued, advancing the round, restoring every motor and putting both banks in good
standing; and one bank's permit is suspended, restoring everything it had isolated, provided the
other bank is left in good standing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every motor that is out of service was isolated by a bank that is still in good
standing and under the permit round that is currently in force, so no suspended bank and no
out-of-date permit ever holds a motor out of service.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Motor claims are never left orphaned for ever; whenever motor claims are
standing with the machine room unclaimed, they are eventually cleared away.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m8p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Desks, Runways, Configs, Nothing, Nobody

ASSUME Nothing \notin Configs

VARIABLES fieldClaim, runwayClaim, published, inHand

vars == <<fieldClaim, runwayClaim, published, inHand>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fieldClaim \in Desks \cup {Nobody}
    /\ runwayClaim \in [Runways -> Desks \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ published \in [Runways -> Configs]
    /\ inHand \in [Runways -> Configs \cup {Nothing}]

Init ==
    /\ fieldClaim = Nobody
    /\ runwayClaim = [r \in Runways |-> Nobody]
    /\ published = [r \in Runways |-> CHOOSE c \in Configs : TRUE]
    /\ inHand = [r \in Runways |-> Nothing]

TakeField(d) ==
    /\ fieldClaim = Nobody
    /\ fieldClaim' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayClaim, published, inHand>>

\* Coarse before fine: no runway claim without the airfield-wide claim.
TakeRunway(d, r) ==
    /\ fieldClaim = d
    /\ runwayClaim[r] = Nobody
    /\ runwayClaim' = [runwayClaim EXCEPT ![r] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldClaim, published, inHand>>

WriteDown(d, r, c) ==
    /\ runwayClaim[r] = d
    /\ inHand[r] = Nothing
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldClaim, runwayClaim, published>>

Publish(d, r) ==
    /\ runwayClaim[r] = d
    /\ inHand[r] # Nothing
    /\ published' = [published EXCEPT ![r] = inHand[r]]
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![r] = Nothing]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldClaim, runwayClaim>>

\* A desk cannot walk away from a runway with an amendment half-made.
GiveBackRunway(d, r) ==
    /\ runwayClaim[r] = d
    /\ inHand[r] = Nothing
    /\ runwayClaim' = [runwayClaim EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldClaim, published, inHand>>

GiveBackField(d) ==
    /\ fieldClaim = d
    /\ \A r \in Runways : runwayClaim[r] # d
    /\ fieldClaim' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayClaim, published, inHand>>

\* The override finishes the amendment on its way out rather than dropping it.
Override(r) ==
    /\ runwayClaim[r] # Nobody
    /\ published' = IF inHand[r] # Nothing
                      THEN [published EXCEPT ![r] = inHand[r]]
                      ELSE published
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![r] = Nothing]
    /\ runwayClaim' = [runwayClaim EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED fieldClaim

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Runways : Override(r)
    \/ \E d \in Desks :
         \/ TakeField(d) \/ GiveBackField(d)
         \/ \E r \in Runways :
              \/ TakeRunway(d, r) \/ Publish(d, r) \/ GiveBackRunway(d, r)
              \/ \E c \in Configs : WriteDown(d, r, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No amendment is ever stranded on a runway nobody is holding.
NoAmendmentStranded ==
    \A r \in Runways : runwayClaim[r] = Nobody => inHand[r] = Nothing

====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator keeps one shared runway record. For each runway the record shows the
configuration currently published to the sectors, and amendments to it are made in two moves: the
amendment is first written down against that runway as the amendment in hand, and it is then
published, which is the move that changes what the record shows and clears the amendment in hand.
An amendment written down but not published is work in progress and is invisible to everybody
reading the record.

Getting at a runway takes two claims, coarse before fine. A sector desk first takes the
airfield-wide claim, which only one desk holds at a time. Holding it, the desk may take a claim on
an individual runway, and only the desk holding a runway's claim may write down or publish an
amendment for it. A desk gives a runway claim back only once it has nothing written down against
that runway, so it can never walk away leaving an amendment half-made. A desk gives the
airfield-wide claim back only once it is holding no runway claims at all.

The watch supervisor holds a privileged override and can prise a runway claim out of a desk's hands
without asking. Because an amendment left written down but unpublished would simply be lost, the
override publishes whatever was written down against that runway as it takes the claim away, and
only then leaves the runway unclaimed.

The full set of actions is: a desk takes the airfield-wide claim when it is free; the desk holding
the airfield-wide claim takes a claim on a free runway; the desk holding a runway's claim writes an
amendment down against that runway, when it has nothing written down there already; the desk
holding a runway's claim publishes what it wrote down, changing the record and clearing the
amendment in hand; a desk gives back a runway claim, only with nothing written down against it; a
desk gives back the airfield-wide claim, only while holding no runway claims; and the supervisor
overrides, publishing whatever was written down against a runway and leaving that runway unclaimed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No runway is ever left unclaimed with an amendment still written down against it
and not yet published, so no amendment is ever lost.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m5p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Seats, Regions, Fabric, NoPlayer, NoSeat, NoProposal, Empty

Proposal == [player : Players, seat : Seats]

VARIABLES book, mySeat, proposal, tally, fabric

vars == <<book, mySeat, proposal, tally, fabric>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NoPlayer}]
    /\ mySeat \in [Players -> Seats \cup {NoSeat}]
    /\ proposal \in Proposal \cup {NoProposal}
    /\ tally \subseteq Regions
    /\ fabric \in [Fabric -> Regions \cup {Empty}]

Carried == Cardinality(tally) * 2 > Cardinality(Regions)

Init ==
    /\ book = [s \in Seats |-> NoPlayer]
    /\ mySeat = [p \in Players |-> NoSeat]
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ fabric = [f \in Fabric |-> Empty]

PutUp(p, s) ==
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ mySeat[p] = NoSeat
    /\ book[s] = NoPlayer
    /\ proposal' = [player |-> p, seat |-> s]
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, mySeat, fabric>>

CastVote(v, f) ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ fabric[f] = Empty
    /\ v \notin tally
    /\ fabric' = [fabric EXCEPT ![f] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, mySeat, proposal, tally>>

\* Votes arrive in any order; one that outlives its proposal is thrown away.
HandOver(f) ==
    /\ fabric[f] # Empty
    /\ IF proposal # NoProposal
         THEN tally' = tally \cup {fabric[f]}
         ELSE tally' = tally
    /\ fabric' = [fabric EXCEPT ![f] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, mySeat, proposal>>

\* Both the seat and the player are re-checked at the moment of seating.
Carry ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ Carried
    /\ book[proposal.seat] = NoPlayer
    /\ mySeat[proposal.player] = NoSeat
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![proposal.seat] = proposal.player]
    /\ mySeat' = [mySeat EXCEPT ![proposal.player] = proposal.seat]
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED fabric

Withdraw ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, mySeat, fabric>>

Leave(p) ==
    /\ mySeat[p] # NoSeat
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![mySeat[p]] = NoPlayer]
    /\ mySeat' = [mySeat EXCEPT ![p] = NoSeat]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, tally, fabric>>

Next ==
    \/ Carry \/ Withdraw
    \/ \E f \in Fabric : HandOver(f)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Leave(p) \/ \E s \in Seats : PutUp(p, s)
    \/ \E v \in Regions, f \in Fabric : CastVote(v, f)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Withdraw)

\* What a player thinks it has and what the book says never come apart.
BookAgreesWithPlayers ==
    \A p \in Players : mySeat[p] # NoSeat => book[mySeat[p]] = p

\* A part-finished ballot is never left standing for ever.
TallyAlwaysClears == (tally # {}) ~> (tally = {})

====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into the lobby's numbered seats. The lobby keeps
a seating book saying which player is in each seat, and every player separately knows which seat it
has been given. A seat holds one player and a player sits in one seat.

Seating is decided by the region servers. The matchmaker puts up one proposal at a time, naming a
player with no seat and a seat the book shows empty. Region servers then vote on the proposal, and
their votes travel over the lobby's message fabric, which carries several votes at once and hands
them over in whatever order it happens to, not the order they were cast. A vote counts only when it
is handed over, and only if the proposal it was cast for is still the proposal on the table; a vote
that arrives after the proposal has gone is discarded rather than being counted towards whatever is
on the table now.

When a strict majority of region servers have votes recorded for the proposal on the table, and the
named seat is still empty and the named player still unseated at that moment, the player is seated:
the book is written and the player is told its seat. Putting a player in clears the proposal and
the recorded votes. A proposal can also be withdrawn, which clears it and the recorded votes
without seating anybody. A seated player can leave, which empties its seat in the book.

The full set of actions is: the matchmaker puts up a proposal naming an unseated player and an
empty seat; a region server casts its vote for the proposal onto a free place on the message
fabric; a vote is handed over off the fabric and recorded, but only if the proposal it was cast for
is still on the table; the proposal is carried and the player seated when a strict majority is
recorded and the seat and player are both still free, clearing the proposal and the votes; the
proposal is withdrawn, clearing it and the votes; and a seated player leaves, emptying its seat.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every player that believes it has a seat is the player the seating book shows in
that seat, so no seat is ever given out to two players at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Recorded votes never stand for ever; whenever any vote has been recorded, the
tally is eventually cleared.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m3p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Routes, Machines, HopperDepth, Product, Nobody, NoMachine

ASSUME HopperDepth < Product

VARIABLES hopper, depot, controller, filling

vars == <<hopper, depot, controller, filling>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ hopper \in [Machines -> 0..Product]
    /\ depot \in 0..Product
    /\ controller \in Routes \cup {Nobody}
    /\ filling \in [Routes -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]

Init ==
    /\ hopper = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ depot = Product
    /\ controller = Nobody
    /\ filling = [r \in Routes |-> NoMachine]

TakeRole(r) ==
    /\ controller = Nobody
    /\ controller' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, depot, filling>>

DropRole ==
    /\ controller # Nobody
    /\ controller' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, depot, filling>>

\* Two routes never work the same machine at the same time.
OpenFill(r, m) ==
    /\ controller # Nobody
    /\ filling[r] = NoMachine
    /\ \A q \in Routes : filling[q] # m
    /\ filling' = [filling EXCEPT ![r] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, depot, controller>>

\* The depth is checked on every single unit, not once per fill.
LoadUnit(r) ==
    /\ filling[r] # NoMachine
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ hopper[filling[r]] < HopperDepth
    /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![filling[r]] = @ + 1]
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<controller, filling>>

CloseFill(r) ==
    /\ filling[r] # NoMachine
    /\ filling' = [filling EXCEPT ![r] = NoMachine]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, depot, controller>>

Vend(m) ==
    /\ hopper[m] > 0
    /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<controller, filling>>

Next ==
    \/ DropRole
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Vend(m)
    \/ \E r \in Routes :
         \/ TakeRole(r) \/ LoadUnit(r) \/ CloseFill(r)
         \/ \E m \in Machines : OpenFill(r, m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No hopper is ever filled past its depth.
HoppersWithinDepth == \A m \in Machines : hopper[m] <= HopperDepth

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Routes = {rtnorth, rtsouth}
    Machines = {vm1, vm2}
    HopperDepth = 2
    Product = 4
    Nobody = nobody
    NoMachine = nomachine

INVARIANT HoppersWithinDepth
nl:
A vending machine network is worked by two restock routes. The routes run independently of each
other but draw their stock from one shared depot, and they fill the same set of machines. Each
machine has a hopper with a fixed depth, and a hopper must never be filled past that depth or the
mechanism jams.

Restocking is authorised by the network's route controller. One route acts as controller at a time;
when there is none, either route can take the role, and the sitting controller can drop it at any
moment, which is how the network carries on when a route's handset goes down. Nothing is restocked
while there is no controller.

A route opens a fill on a machine that the other route is not already filling, and then loads
product into it one unit at a time. Each unit loaded comes out of the shared depot and goes into
that machine's hopper, and a unit is only loaded if the hopper is below its depth at that moment.
The route closes the fill when it is done. Product sold out of a machine goes back to the depot as
the empties are collected, so the network's product neither appears from nowhere nor disappears.

The full set of actions is: a route takes the controller role when there is none; the sitting
controller drops the role; a route opens a fill on a machine that the other route is not filling,
provided there is a controller; a route loads one unit from the depot into the machine it is
filling, provided that hopper is below its depth; a route closes its fill; and a machine vends one
unit, which returns that unit to the depot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No machine's hopper ever holds more units than the hopper's depth allows.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m1p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS SiteCount, Tickets, MaxBatch, NoSite

Sites == 1..SiteCount

\* The ring order the permit travels in.
Downstream(s) == IF s = SiteCount THEN 1 ELSE s + 1

VARIABLES banked, inPlay, carrying, permitAt, onLink

vars == <<banked, inPlay, carrying, permitAt, onLink>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ banked \in [Sites -> 0..Tickets]
    /\ inPlay \in [Sites -> 0..Tickets]
    /\ carrying \in 0..Tickets
    /\ permitAt \in Sites \cup {NoSite}
    /\ onLink \in Sites \cup {NoSite}

RECURSIVE Total(_, _)
Total(S, f) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[s] + Total(S \ {s}, f)

Init ==
    /\ banked = [s \in Sites |-> IF s = 1 THEN Tickets ELSE 0]
    /\ inPlay = [s \in Sites |-> 0]
    /\ carrying = 0
    /\ permitAt = 1
    /\ onLink = NoSite

\* Picked-up tickets leave the bank at once and land only when set down.
PickUp(s, k) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ carrying = 0
    /\ banked[s] >= k
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ - k]
    /\ carrying' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inPlay, permitAt, onLink>>

SetDown(s) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ carrying > 0
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ + carrying]
    /\ carrying' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inPlay, permitAt, onLink>>

Commit(s, k) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ banked[s] >= k
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ - k]
    /\ inPlay' = [inPlay EXCEPT ![s] = @ + k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, permitAt, onLink>>

ReturnToBank(s, k) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ inPlay[s] >= k
    /\ inPlay' = [inPlay EXCEPT ![s] = @ - k]
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ + k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, permitAt, onLink>>

LetGo(s) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ permitAt' = NoSite
    /\ onLink' = Downstream(s)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<banked, inPlay, carrying>>

Arrive ==
    /\ onLink # NoSite
    /\ permitAt' = onLink
    /\ onLink' = NoSite
    /\ UNCHANGED <<banked, inPlay, carrying>>

LetGoSome == \E s \in Sites : LetGo(s)

Next ==
    \/ Arrive \/ LetGoSome
    \/ \E s \in Sites :
         \/ SetDown(s)
         \/ \E k \in 1..MaxBatch : PickUp(s, k) \/ Commit(s, k) \/ ReturnToBank(s, k)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(LetGoSome)

\* Every ticket is banked somewhere, in play somewhere, or on the permit.
TicketsConserved ==
    Total(Sites, banked) + Total(Sites, inPlay) + carrying = Tickets

\* No site sits on the permit for ever.
PermitKeepsMoving ==
    \A s \in Sites : (permitAt = s) ~> (permitAt # s)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    SiteCount = 3
    Tickets = 3
    MaxBatch = 2
    NoSite = 0

INVARIANT TicketsConserved

PROPERTY PermitKeepsMoving
nl:
A multiplayer game runs two lobby shards that are otherwise independent but share one pool of match
tickets. Tickets are the thing that lets a match run, and the operator neither mints nor destroys
them during a season, so at every moment every ticket is in exactly one place: banked at the ticket
pool or at one of the two shards, committed to a match in play at one of them, or riding on the
wire with the transfer permit.

Only one site may move tickets at a time, and the right to move them is a single permit that goes
round the three sites in a fixed ring order. The permit is either sitting at a site or travelling
down the link to the next site round, never at two sites and never nowhere. The site holding the
permit may pick up a batch of its banked tickets onto the permit, and may set down onto its own
bank whatever the permit is carrying. Picking up takes the tickets out of that site's bank the
moment it happens; they only land somewhere again when they are set down.

Also under the permit, a site may commit some of its banked tickets to matches in play, and may
return tickets from finished matches back to its bank.

The full set of actions is: the site holding the permit picks up a batch of its banked tickets onto
the permit, when the permit is carrying nothing; the site holding the permit sets down onto its own
bank whatever the permit is carrying; the site holding the permit commits a batch of its banked
tickets to matches in play; the site holding the permit returns a batch of tickets from play to its
bank; the site holding the permit lets it go onto the link to the next site round the ring; and a
permit travelling on a link arrives at the site it was sent to.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The tickets banked across the three sites, plus those committed to matches in play,
plus whatever the permit is carrying, always add up to exactly the season's fixed ticket count.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No site keeps the permit for ever; whenever a site is holding it, the permit
eventually moves off that site.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m6p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Scanners, Channels, LeaseTicks, LastNumber, Nobody, Idle, Empty

Stamped == [by : Scanners, number : 0..LastNumber]

VARIABLES owner, ticks, number, setting, busbar

vars == <<owner, ticks, number, setting, busbar>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Scanners \cup {Nobody}
    /\ ticks \in 0..LeaseTicks
    /\ number \in 0..LastNumber
    /\ setting \in Stamped \cup {Idle}
    /\ busbar \in [Channels -> Stamped \cup {Empty}]

BusClear == \A c \in Channels : busbar[c] = Empty

Init ==
    /\ owner = Nobody
    /\ ticks = 0
    /\ number = 0
    /\ setting = Idle
    /\ busbar = [c \in Channels |-> Empty]

\* Every grant takes a fresh number, which is what dates the old ones.
Grant(n) ==
    /\ owner = Nobody
    /\ number < LastNumber
    /\ owner' = n
    /\ ticks' = LeaseTicks
    /\ number' = number + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<setting, busbar>>

\* Running out leaves nobody owning the chute and nothing set on it.
Tick ==
    /\ ticks > 0
    /\ ticks' = ticks - 1
    /\ owner' = IF ticks = 1 THEN Nobody ELSE owner
    /\ setting' = IF ticks = 1 THEN Idle ELSE setting
    /\ UNCHANGED <<number, busbar>>

Renew(n) ==
    /\ owner = n
    /\ ticks > 0
    /\ ticks' = LeaseTicks
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, number, setting, busbar>>

Post(n, c) ==
    /\ owner = n
    /\ ticks > 0
    /\ busbar[c] = Empty
    /\ busbar' = [busbar EXCEPT ![c] = [by |-> n, number |-> number]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ticks, number, setting>>

\* Name, lease number and a running lease must all still line up on arrival.
Apply(c) ==
    /\ busbar[c] # Empty
    /\ LET m == busbar[c] IN
         /\ IF owner = m.by /\ number = m.number /\ ticks > 0
              THEN setting' = m
              ELSE setting' = setting
         /\ busbar' = [busbar EXCEPT ![c] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ticks, number>>

Wipe(n) ==
    /\ owner = n
    /\ setting # Idle
    /\ setting' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ticks, number, busbar>>

HandBack(n) ==
    /\ owner = n
    /\ owner' = Nobody
    /\ ticks' = 0
    /\ setting' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<number, busbar>>

RestartNumbering ==
    /\ number = LastNumber
    /\ owner = Nobody
    /\ setting = Idle
    /\ BusClear
    /\ number' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ticks, setting, busbar>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick \/ RestartNumbering
    \/ \E c \in Channels : Apply(c)
    \/ \E n \in Scanners :
         \/ Grant(n) \/ Renew(n) \/ Wipe(n) \/ HandBack(n)
         \/ \E c \in Channels : Post(n, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing governs the chute except the owner of the lease running right now.
SettingBackedByLiveLease ==
    setting # Idle =>
        (owner # Nobody /\ setting.by = owner /\ setting.number = number /\ ticks > 0)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Scanners = {scnA, scnB}
    Channels = {fb1, fb2}
    LeaseTicks = 2
    LastNumber = 2
    Nobody = nobody
    Idle = idle
    Empty = empty

INVARIANT SettingBackedByLiveLease
nl:
An airport baggage router has one oversize chute whose diversion setting says where oversize items
are being sent. The setting is only ever written by whichever scanner node currently owns the
chute, and ownership is leased rather than permanent.

A lease is granted to a node when the chute is unowned, and each grant carries a fresh lease number,
one higher than the last. A lease runs for a fixed count of table ticks and counts down; the owner
can renew it while it is still running, which puts the count back to full without changing the lease
number. When the count reaches nothing the lease is over: the chute becomes unowned and its
diversion setting is wiped, because a setting with nobody behind it is not a setting anybody should
be routing to. The owner can also hand the lease back early, which does the same thing, and can
wipe the setting itself while still holding the lease.

Diversion instructions are not applied where they are written. The owner puts an instruction onto
the router's field bus, stamped with its own name and its lease number. The bus carries several
instructions at once and hands them to the chute in whatever order it gets to them, not the order
they were written, so an instruction can arrive long after the lease it was written under has run
out or been handed on. The chute applies an instruction only if the name on it is the node that
owns the chute right now, the lease number on it is the lease number running right now, and that
lease has not run out. Anything else is thrown away on arrival.

Lease numbers do not run for ever. When the numbering has reached its last value and the chute is
unowned, its setting wiped and the bus completely clear, the numbering starts again from the
beginning.

The full set of actions is: a node is granted the lease on the unowned chute, taking a fresh lease
number and a full count; the table ticks, counting the lease down and, if that exhausts it, leaving
the chute unowned with its setting wiped; the owner renews its lease back to a full count; the
owner puts a stamped instruction onto a free place on the field bus; the chute takes an instruction
off the bus and applies it only if the name, the lease number and the running lease all match,
throwing it away otherwise; the owner wipes the diversion setting; the owner hands the lease back
early, wiping the setting; and the lease numbering restarts once it has run out with nothing owned,
nothing set and the bus clear.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the chute carries a diversion setting, it was written by the node that
owns the chute right now, under the lease number running right now, and that lease has not run out,
so no lapsed owner and no out-of-date instruction ever governs where oversize items go.
